title: Handle swallowed exceptions — add logging to empty catch blocks across services
description:
## Source
SonarQube static analysis audit (`Data/Pages/audits/ms-sonar-static-analysis-7-26-26.md`); also violates AGENTS.md Rule E-3

## Findings
12 instances where exceptions are caught but the catch block is empty or the exception path is not logged:

**C# (9 instances):**
- `ChatServices.cs` (L423-424, L811-812, L1419-1420, L1435-1436) — 4 instances
- `MemoryGovernanceServices.cs` (L77-78) — 1 instance
- `MaintenanceAgentServices.cs` (L1794, L1850) — 2 instances
- `SemanticEmbeddingPrewarmService.cs` (L86) — 1 instance

**Python (2 instances):**
- `harness.py` (L370, L467)

**PowerShell (1 instance):**
- `Scripts/Import-OpenTasksFromWorkbench.ps1` (L47)

## Impact
Empty catch blocks silently swallow exceptions, making debugging extremely difficult. This directly violates AGENTS.md Rule E-3 ("Never Swallow Exceptions").

## Action Required
Add `LogWarning` or `LogError` logging to all empty catch blocks with context about the operation being attempted. Follow the safe catch pattern: `catch (Exception ex) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested) { logger?.LogWarning(ex, "Non-fatal error in {Context}: {Message}", ...); }`

## Effort
~30min

## Priority
P1 — Reliability

comments.body: 2026-08-08 deep-dive confirmed two concrete silent visibility failures for this broad logging task: SecurityServices JSONL mirror catches discard exceptions without health signal, and malformed maintenance proposal JSON is converted to null and omitted. Preserve file identity and exception context in diagnostics.
